caminhos.title: Three ways in. You can stop at the first.
caminhos.intro: Buying just for yourself is a complete option, not a step towards something else. Sharing the products and building a team are choices, never conditions.

items.title: Buying just for yourself
items.text: The beauty products you already buy, at a discount. In the UK, signing up is free and gives you 15 % off your first order; with the Beauty Entrepreneur fee of £19 for the first year, you get 20 % off every order. No minimum order and no obligation to buy: you order when you want, and that's it.

items.title: A little extra from people who already buy beauty
items.text: Your sister, a colleague, the neighbour across the landing: they already buy creams and perfume somewhere. If they order through you, Oriflame rewards those purchases. No minimum order, no stock, at your own pace, and you can stop whenever you like.

items.title: A business of your own, with a team
items.text: An independent business: your own customers, inviting people and helping them sell, with {leader_name} beside you from day one. The first months are slow, and the simulation shows that with no make-up on.

passos.title: How it works
passos.intro: Four steps. To find out, the first one is enough.

diagnostico_cta.title: Numbers first. Then you decide.
diagnostico_cta.text: You've been sold “extra income” before, with holiday photos and not a single sum done. This works the other way round: the numbers come first, worked out from your time, your contacts and the official plan for your country. The decision comes later, and it's yours.

lider.title: I'm {leader_name}, and I'm the one who replies.
lider.fallback_bio: I'm an independent Oriflame partner: I work for myself and I don't speak for the brand. I'll be straight with you: if you sign up with my code, you join my team and I benefit too. That's why I'd rather show you the numbers before we talk, the cautious scenario included. If you only want to buy for yourself at a discount, that's a complete option and I'll help you just the same. If you still have questions after the simulation, message me. I reply myself, with no rush and no pressure.

items.q: How much does it cost to join, and how much do I save?
items.a: In the UK, signing up as a VIP is free, with no minimum order, and gives you 15 % off your first order. As a Beauty Entrepreneur, for £19 for the first year and £10 a year after that, you get 20 % off every order, with no stock and no compulsory purchases. The simulation uses the 20 % and doesn't deduct the fee. In Portugal sign-up is free; in Spain and France there is also an annual fee. {leader_name} will show you the terms for your country before you sign up.

items.q: Do I have to sell or invite anyone?
items.a: No. Buying just for yourself is a complete option. There's no minimum order and no compulsory purchase: you order when you want, at your own pace. Sharing the products and inviting people are your decisions, and neither is needed to get the discount.

It's a fair question. The heart of this is buying products: Oriflame's discount and rewards come from orders of beauty products. The annual fee is charged by Oriflame and gives access to its rewards plan; people who build a team earn when the people in their team buy. The simulation shows every assumption, so you can see where each number comes from.

items.q: What does {leader_name} get if I sign up?
items.a: If you sign up with {leader_name}'s code, you join {leader_name}'s team, and your purchases benefit {leader_name} too, under the rules of Oriflame's plan. Prices and terms are Oriflame's own, and {leader_name} doesn't charge you anything for the support.

No. They're an estimate built from your answers and the official plan Oriflame publishes for your country (October 2026), with every assumption shown. Team bonuses are left out, because Oriflame doesn't publish the tier table. Your real result depends on your time and your sales. The simulation covers Portugal, Spain, France and the UK.

items.q: Is this the official Oriflame website?
items.a: No. This page belongs to {brand_name}, an independent Oriflame partner who works for themselves. The products, orders, prices and terms are Oriflame's own.

No. It isn't a job, part-time or otherwise, and there's no salary. It's an independent business, with the tax obligations of your country. If you start selling, it's best to check your situation with an accountant; {leader_name} will walk you through the first steps.

It's used to email you the report and, if you ask, for {leader_name} to reply to you on WhatsApp. It isn't sold or used for advertising, and nobody calls you unless you ask. You can ask to see or delete it at any time, under UK GDPR.

cta_final.title: A year from now, you'll have bought beauty products anyway.
cta_final.text: The question is whether you paid full price for them. See the numbers with {brand_name}: 3 minutes, free, and the decision is still yours.

consumidora.label: Buying just for yourself, at a discount
consumidora.analysis: From your answers, what you're after is simple: keep using the products you like and pay less for them. That's a complete option in itself, not a compulsory step towards something else. With the discount, part of what you already spend on beauty each month stays in your pocket. In the UK, signing up is free and gives you 15 % off your first order; with the £19 first-year fee, you get 20 % off every order, which is the discount the simulation uses, without deducting the fee. If, over time, one or two people close to you ask you to order for them too, you can, and that could help cover part of your own spending. But you don't have to, now or later. There's no minimum order and no compulsory purchase. The most useful thing in the first few weeks is to get to know the catalogue calmly, try the products you already use and compare them with what you paid before. Real figures depend on Oriflame's official terms in your country. The next step is a conversation, if you'd like one, not a commitment.

rendimento_extra.label: A little extra, at your own pace
rendimento_extra.analysis: You said you're looking for some extra income that fits the life you already have, and this analysis was built to that measure. The hours per week and the contacts you mentioned weigh more in the result than enthusiasm or someone else's example. So use the likely scenario as your reference and the cautious one as a realistic starting point. The main lever isn't always finding new customers, it's having customers who order again. Two or three happy, well-looked-after people are worth more than lots of one-off conversations. In the first months, it's normal to move slowly while you get to know the products and build a short, regular routine. Sharing is always your decision, with people you already know and at your own pace, and you can stop whenever you like. Remember this is an estimate: real results depend on your time, your sales and the official terms in your country. The next step is a conversation, if you'd like one, not a commitment.

construtora_negocio.label: Building a business of your own
construtora_negocio.analysis: You chose to build a business, and the first thing to know is where the potential lies: less in your own sales and more in building a team, that is, inviting people and helping them sell well. Not everyone you invite will want to sell, and that's normal. Your sales experience and the way you use social media can speed that process up, but they don't replace it. It's worth being clear about the start: the first months are usually slow, because you're building a customer base, learning the plan and supporting your first people. The simulation reflects that ramp, and the ambitious scenario only makes sense if the team grows steadily. Oriflame's team bonuses are left out of these numbers, because the tier table isn't published. Building a team is about support, not persuasion: the right people stay when they see method and honesty. {leader_name} supports that journey from day one. Real results depend on your work and the official terms in your country. The next step is a conversation, if you'd like one, not a commitment.
